svg.title: Mockup 07: fixes, auto-fix rules, logs
svg.text: 07 · Fixes: typed actions, auto-fix rules that try first, the action log, and a part's last lines (superadmin)
The executor is designed new: every action has a name, a right, a guard and an audit entry. No free-text command exists; the ops sidecar may only restart, inspect and read logs.
Use case: the superadmin decides which fixes may run by themselves, checks what ran overnight, and reads a slow part's redacted log lines
A · Fixes at 1280 px: the rules, then the log
What may run by itself, and everything that ran, by whom.
When a screen is online but has not drawn its zone for 60 s, or repeats one error 3 times.
Wait 5 min between tries · at most 3 in 30 min · then one "gave up" alert
When its client is down for 1 min and Discord still accepts its token.
Wait 2 min between tries · at most 3 in 30 min · never with a refused token
Restart a part that is down
When a part is down for 2 min while Postgres and Valkey are ok.
Waits while any live event has a takeover, an emergency or a cast on air
Restart a part: turned on per part, from its card in Stack health. Never for a muted subject (E7).
The log is the audit log's fix entries: kept as the audit is, actors as audit references (O4).
B · A part's last lines, redacted (the sidecar's logs verb)
Redacted by the kit's patterns before they leave the sidecar (D13). Newest last.

svg.text: C · An auto-fix that gave up

g.text: Three reconnects did not hold. Discord refuses
the bot's token: someone must set a new one in
Gave up: no more tries until it recovers

svg.text: Three typed auto-fix rules for step 8, the legacy engine's rules as their spec: a trigger, a
wait, a cap per 30 min, one "gave up" alert, never while muted (D11, E7).
Every fix, by a person or by a rule, is one row of the audit log with its result; "waited" and
"gave up" are rows, not state changes (legacy P4).
A refused token is never retried in a loop: Discord blocks an address that keeps failing
(bot.md), so the rule stops and asks a person.
